items.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewer mentions 'Shadow Wilson' as an example of people the interviewee might have anecdotes about, but the interviewee does not respond to this specific mention or provide any personal interaction details regarding Wilson.

ctx.x: Right, but that’s later. In terms of your going to the clubs and your intimate friendships with these people and being around it. Can you tell us any anecdotes or experiences that we can learn from, just about how you saw it happen, by the people asking for money, or nodding out, or changing – or Shadow Wilson, or people who for some reason . . .

You mention asking for money. Bud Powell, who was obviously an extraordinary pianist – really a pianist-composer, because that’s what that’s all about. You just don’t improvise out of thin air. But when he was on heroin, he was worse than pathetic. He’d come up to me and say, “Can I have a dollar? two dollars? five dollars?” I’m thinking, here is this genius, so to speak, and look what happens to him. I didn’t have too much experience with that kind of thing. You didn’t expect it, but you weren’t surprised when…
